Apple is reportedly planning to release new products on October 13. Based on the timing of previous October events, the following estimates when the company might announce the event date.

Will Apple hold an October event?

While the timing of Apple's September events has historically been predictable, October events are far less consistent, with both the dates and advance notice varying significantly.

Since 2010, Apple has held only ten October events, the most recent being the Halloween-themed 'Scary Fast' event on the evening of October 30, 2023.

Below is how far in advance Apple has announced each of its October events since 2010:

Year Event Announcement date Event date 2023 “Scary Fast” Tuesday, October 24 Monday, October 30 2021 “Unleashed” Tuesday, October 12 Monday, October 18 2020 “Hi, Speed” Tuesday, October 6 Tuesday, October 13 2018 “There’s more in the making” Thursday, October 18 Tuesday, October 30 2016 “Hello again” Wednesday, October 19 Thursday, October 27 2014 “It’s been way too long” Wednesday, October 8 Thursday, October 16 2013 “We still have a lot to cover” Tuesday, October 15 Tuesday, October 22 2012 “We’ve got a little more to show you” Tuesday, October 16 Tuesday, October 23 2011 “Let’s talk iPhone” Tuesday, September 27 Tuesday, October 4 2010 “Back to the Mac” Wednesday, October 13 Wednesday, October 20

However, Bloomberg previously reported that Apple plans to unveil its long-rumored smart home hub, a new-generation HomePod mini, and an Apple TV 4K with all-new Siri AI features on Tuesday, October 13, though it did not specify whether the company would hold an event to announce these products.

If there is indeed an event, Apple could announce the date as early as next Monday (October 5), but no later than Wednesday, October 7.

It is also worth mentioning that Apple is expected to announce an iPad mini with an OLED display, a new iMac, and several new MacBook Pro models in 2026, including versions with touch functionality. Whether these products will be unveiled at the same event, a separate event, or simply through press releases remains unknown.

Looking back, Apple released new Macs via press releases on three consecutive days in October 2024; in October 2025, it skipped an event entirely and directly launched the M5 chip along with new iPad Pro, MacBook Pro, and Apple Vision Pro models.

By comparison, Apple has held only one event in November, back in 2020, when the 'One More Thing' event unveiled the first Macs powered by the M1 Apple Silicon chip.

Of course, 2020 was an unusual year for Apple — the COVID-19 pandemic disrupted the company's usual schedule, with WWDC being held unusually in late June, followed by separate events in September and October.

What new products do you think Apple will announce at its rumored October event? Share your thoughts in the comments.
